text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A records office logs intake forms, assigns identifiers, timestamps, and file locations for submitted documents. It tracks associated accounts, channels of delivery, and revision history. Staff annotate fields, attach exhibits, and route records to designated review queues per standing procedure.

2) What occurred: The actor created a draft agreement document containing a payment-schedule field and a status field marked as "settled." The actor registered two account records under distinct identifiers, linked them in a relationship-matrix exhibit, and populated shared address fields with matching values. The actor attached a dated itinerary document, a set of dated photographic exhibits, and a correspondence log spanning multiple months. The actor prepared an interview-preparation outline document and filed it under a coaching subfile. The actor set the payment-disclosure field in the application package to "none" while the draft agreement remained in the same folder, and routed the package through a third-party channel with a forwarding note.

3) Materials/access observed: One draft agreement (payment schedule, status field), two linked account records, one relationship-matrix exhibit, one dated itinerary, a dated photographic exhibit set, one correspondence log, one interview-preparation outline, one application package with a payment-disclosure field set to "none," one forwarding note, and one third-party delivery channel.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Matching address fields across two distinct account identifiers; a payment-schedule field coexisting with a disclosure field set to "none"; a subfile structure (draft, exhibits, preparation outline) within a single folder; a correspondence log with consecutive monthly dates; a delivery channel distinct from the primary filing channel; and a forwarding note attached to the routed package.
